desc: Derive the basic multilinearity observation and identify zero-weight/inverse pitfalls.
Implement and validate the exact transfer-matrix segment tree for grids with minimum dimension at most three.
Investigate separator/r-division boundary-transfer representations; straightforward explicit Schur-complement maintenance has linear worst-case update cost.
Establish that the current code passes both public sample tests, while its general branch remains worst-case O(HWQ).
Disprove the naive linear-size contraction theorem for a connected update walk, using the dense staircase counterexample.

Find a structured dynamic planar-DAG representation or alternative invariant which handles dense marked-to-marked staircase interactions without explicitly materializing them, with proven sublinear update time.
Derive a complete arbitrary-dimension dynamic algorithm exploiting the adjacent cursor walk, including precise time and memory complexity and zero-safe modular arithmetic.
Investigate structured sparse transfer products or lazy Woodbury maintenance for a non-separator arbitrary-dimension update structure.
Prove correctness, including zero values and updates to endpoints, for the selected representation.
Implement the resulting algorithm in Python and validate it on public samples and constraint-scale complexity.
